title: identity-retention: the pre-registered pipeline for the identity-retention fraction in paired tumor-adjacent expression contrasts, with the retentionfrac package

creators.name: Nam, Soon Woo
creators.affiliation: Incheon St. Mary's Hospital, College of Medicine, The Catholic University of Korea

description:
Deposit notice. Two earlier Zenodo versions of this archive carry a label that does not match their files. The versions labeled v1.3.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23052241) and v1.3.1 (10.5281/zenodo.23054376) both deposited the v1.2.4 tree of 259 files, because the intended content never reached the source repository before the tag was created. Zenodo versions cannot be withdrawn, so those records remain and are annotated. Everything intended for v1.3.0 and v1.3.1 is in this version, v1.3.2, including the held-out cohort predictions, the protocol deviations, the cholangiocarcinoma results and the closure notice. Section 7 of docs/CLOSURE_2026-09-30.md records the incident in full. The concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22658669 is unaffected.

Closure notice, 30 September 2026 (v1.3.2). This line of work was closed and the article it supported was not published. Read docs/CLOSURE_2026-09-30.md first: it gives the publication history, the two final controls, the claims withdrawn, and the one claim the data support. Earlier text in README.md is left in place and that file marks it.

What is withdrawn. The claim that the 22-gene composite's sign is arbitrary is withdrawn as stated: three of four proteome composites are statistically significant when recomputed from the raw matrices, and the defensible statement is that the sign is unstable across cohorts and across quantification pipelines applied to the same raw files. The claim about plasma proteins and albumin is withdrawn: against the background of its own matrix the plasma class rises in two proteomes and falls in two. The held-out confirmation holds in the primary quantification of that cohort and fails in one of its two sensitivity quantifications.

What survives. A module of urea cycle and gluconeogenic enzymes (CPS1, OTC, ARG1, PCK1) falls further than almost anything else measured, in four independent paired liver proteomes and two tumor types. The fall survives restriction to proteins detected in both arms of every pair, is 26 to 230 times larger than any compositional renormalization could produce, and in the one cohort with matched transcript and protein measurements these enzymes are among the most tightly concordant genes in the proteome while ALB is at the 0.4th percentile of 6,203. Down-regulation of the urea cycle in hepatocellular carcinoma is already published as a proteomic signature, which is why this was not pursued further.

Contents. Analysis code, gene sets, derived result files and the locked protocol for the study How much of a tumor expression signature survives adjustment for the dominant tumor-adjacent axis? A pre-registered measure in three tissues and its failure to transfer between a transcriptome and a proteome. 764 paired samples across eight datasets, with each matrix's premises checked before any contrast was computed and two matrices reported as not testable rather than analyzed. Every failed prediction is deposited alongside the ones that held. Includes retentionfrac 1.0.1, a one-function Python package that computes the identity-retention fraction with a bootstrap interval and refuses to return a value when the identity premise or the ratio-stability guard fails.

The measure is named for the covariate used to compute it and not for a mechanism. Under amendment 6ae a covariate drawn at random and matched to the identity score on the size of its own paired tumor shift removes as much as the identity score does, so the quantity measures alignment with a large paired tumor-adjacent axis rather than anything specific to differentiation.

SHA256SUMS.txt at the root lists every file in the archive; shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt verifies the deposit.
